sources.title: Metacat: A Self-Watching Cognitive Architecture for Analogy-Making
sources.access: Indexed author abstract; direct page returned bot verification

sources.title: A self-watching model of analogy-making and perception

implemented: Copycat constructs context-sensitive mappings in a letter-string microworld. Metacat adds monitoring of its own activity and episodic recall; sample runs are reported.
learned: Temporary contextual adjustments in Copycat, but no durable learning across runs; Metacat adds episodic mechanisms, not established acquisition of general concepts.
designed: Fixed Slipnet concept inventory and topology, codelet operations, input domain and coherence biases.
limit: Copycat authors explicitly state that each run restarts from the same initial state and creates no permanent concepts. Metacat sample runs cannot establish unrestricted generalization or introspective experience.
ora: Distinguish transient state-dependent behavior from durable acquisition; avoid treating within-run flexibility as proof of learning.

sources.title: Infant-like Social Interactions between a Robot and a Human Caregiver
sources.access: MIT author publication abstract and publisher metadata

sources.title: Sociable machines: expressive social exchange between humans and robots
sources.access: MIT institutional thesis metadata and abstract; full thesis not reviewed

implemented: Physical robot adjusts its expressive behavior during human and toy-mediated interaction; author reports social exchange evaluations.
learned: These records establish reported regulation of interactions and conditions intended to support learning; durable acquisition of new cognitive abilities is not established here.
designed: Perception, attention, drives, emotional displays and action selection; caregiver supplies social context.
limit: Social signals that observers interpret as emotion or intention do not establish subjective feelings or autonomous developmental learning.
ora: Behavioral appearance is insufficient; distinguish internal functional state, observer interpretation and durable acquisition.

sources.authors: Sao Mai Nguyen; Serena Ivaldi; Natalia Lyubova; Alain Droniou; Damien Gérardeaux-Viret; David Filliat; Vincent Padois; Olivier Sigaud; Pierre-Yves Oudeyer
sources.title: Learning to recognize objects through curiosity-driven manipulation with the iCub humanoid robot
sources.access: Author publication list and abstract; HAL id hal-00919674; related institutional activity report https://rex-radar.inria.fr/report/2012/flowers/uid143.html

implemented: iCub active perception experiments with object manipulation and human assistance within MACSi; learning of object recognition is reported.
learned: Incrementally acquired visual object representations through active exploration.
designed: Sensorimotor interfaces, elementary actions, perception pipeline, curiosity criterion, social interaction channels; see https://flowers.inria.fr/active-learning/ for the lab's explicit learning-progress reward principle.
limit: Full quantitative comparisons and controls remain unreviewed; object recognition is not evidence of unrestricted developmental intelligence. MACSi uses iCub and is not an independent platform lineage.
ora: Prior art for separating acquired representations from provided actions and learning objectives.

sources.authors: Michael T. Cox; Zohreh Alavi; Dustin Dannenhauer; Vahid Eyorokon; Hector Muñoz-Avila; Don Perlis
sources.title: MIDCA: A Metacognitive, Integrated Dual-Cycle Architecture for Self-Regulated Autonomy
sources.access: Author PDF selected architecture, performance and conclusion sections; page images 3712, 3716 and 3718 checked

implemented: Dual-cycle architecture, comparison of three approaches to goal formation in simulated tower construction with disturbances; one implemented meta-level planner-failure response.
learned: Statistical goal generation uses examples of relevant and irrelevant states; causal interpretation approach generates corrective goals from discrepancies. No evidence that underlying values are learned independently.
designed: Domain predicates, operators, planning machinery, scoring, explanation structures and meta-level discrepancy response; paper states meta-level explanation generation was future work and discrepancy-to-goal mapping was direct.
limit: Causal approach outperforms reactive alternatives in the reported scenario, not evidence of spontaneous value formation. Exact funding acknowledgements are not independent award acceptance records.
ora: Distinguish context-generated subgoals from origins of objectives; distinguish a predefined recovery response from newly learned causal explanation.

sources.authors: Ben Goertzel; Joel Pitt; Jared Wigmore; Nil Geisweiller; Zhenhua Cai; Ruiting Lian; Deheng Huang; Gino Yu
sources.title: Cognitive Synergy Between Procedural and Declarative Learning in the Control of Animated and Robotic Agents Using the OpenCogPrime AGI Architecture
sources.access: AAAI primary PDF indexed text, selected architecture/limitations; screenshot attempt returned access interstitial; original article copyright AAAI 2011

implemented: Authors report research applications to virtual agents and humanoid robots; discuss integration of probabilistic declarative inference and procedural learning. Their description distinguishes prior narrow evaluations from the larger research objective.
learned: Reported procedural and declarative learning in bounded applications; magnitude of benefit from integration not established by reviewed excerpts.
designed: Memory graph, learning and inference algorithms, mechanisms allocating attention and goals, interfaces.
limit: 2011 authors explicitly state contemporary functionality was far from child/adult-level ambitions; low-level sensorimotor knowledge not handled by the then-current core. No full causal synergy comparison audited.
ora: Integration is a prior hypothesis rather than proof that general intelligence follows. Keep mechanism-specific evidence separate from anticipated system-level capabilities.
